claims.text: The pristine PGM-based nanoscale catalyst has a relatively uniform metallic surface with minimal pre-existing oxides or hydroxides.
A thermal-electrochemical pretreatment will induce surface restructuring while maintaining overall catalyst integrity.
The pretreatment will produce co-existing metallic and oxide/hydroxide surface domains.
The heterogeneous domains will occur particularly at surface step and edge sites.
Dynamic restructuring creates active boundaries between metallic and oxidized regions.
Metallic surface sites promote ethanol adsorption.
Oxide/hydroxide surface regions facilitate proton transfer.
Oxide/hydroxide surface regions stabilize ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The interaction of metallic and oxidized regions lowers energy barriers for complete ethanol oxidation.
Complete ethanol oxidation is an overall 12-electron and 12-proton process.
Mixed metallic and oxide/hydroxide sites increase catalytic turnover.
Mixed metallic and oxide/hydroxide sites improve durability by mitigating surface poisoning.
Pretreated catalysts will exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation current densities than untreated catalysts.
Pretreated catalysts will exhibit higher Faradaic efficiency for complete ethanol oxidation than untreated catalysts.
Pretreated catalysts will remain more stable during prolonged ethanol oxidation than untreated catalysts.
The proposed mechanism applies under aqueous proton-conducting conditions when the surface can dynamically restructure.
Alloying or surface inhibitors that restrict atomic mobility may prevent the proposed mechanism.
The proposed mechanism may fail in reaction environments that do not involve proton-coupled electron transfer.
Prior reports documented strong ethanol-oxidation performance for nanoscale PGM catalysts.
